_about: THE PORT'S OWN RULES, laid over the web's tables (content/rules.json, which the export writes and the parity replay reads alone). Each block says why. Rules.data() merges this in for the game; Rules.web_only (the parity runner) leaves it out.
_crates: Crate rebalance, 2026-10-01 (Kong, revised the same day). A crate stays a 1% chance on every cast in every water; depth decides WHICH crates can come up, and no water gives every tier (the shallows only wooden and metal, the abyss only gold and diamond, the ancient deep diamond and the ancient chest half and half). Each tier is strictly better than the one below. Cosmetics stay a small chance in every crate (1 to 5%); a better crate reaches RARER cosmetics, not more of them: each cosmetic in the web's pool has a band (cosmeticRarity), and each tier draws only from its bands (cosmeticBands).
_pets: Each crate its own set (Kong, 2026-10-01): every pet belongs to exactly one crate tier, so a crate's collection is its own pets and its cosmetic bands, and the gold-coloured pets live in the deepest crates. The chance of a pet per crate (crate.petChance) is the web's; which pet is drawn from that crate's own list, each weighted by its share of the web's whole pet roll. Duplicates can still come up.
_rarity: Pet chance per crate, 1% to 4% by tier (Kong, 2026-10-01): wooden 1, metal 1.5, gold 2, diamond 3, ancient 4 (the web's 0.5 / 1 / 2 / 4 / 10). Cosmetics unchanged.
_levels: Levels give upgrades and unlocks, not money (Kong, 2026-10-01). No level pays doubloons, and no level pays gems (gems are being retired from both builds). Fishing levels raise the fish hold for free (Medium at 10, Large at 20, Cargo at 30, Deep at 45, Grand at 60; Titan, Leviathan and Kraken stay bought), so levelRewardMax runs to 100. FISHING levels raise the sailing upgrades for free too (shipUpgrades: the hull's second tier at Fishing 10 and third at 25, the rudder's second at 15, the rig's second at 20), while Navigation has no way to grow in the port; the rest are bought, each behind a Fishing level (levelGates.ship). The small bait at levels is kept. Bait a level gives that is not yet unlocked at that level is given instead at the level that unlocks it (a 0 here clears the web's gift).
_gates: Everything bought is tied to a Fishing level, RuneScape style (Kong, 2026-10-01; fishing only for now, the ship's upgrades wait for Navigation). levelGates: bait, the bought holds (Titan 75, Leviathan 85, Kraken 95), the Auto Caster (25); the portal to a water needs that water's level. BOATS COME ONLY FROM FISHING CRATES: every boat that was sold is crate-only and sits in the crate cosmetic pool with a band; the boats earned by level or achievement (ice, celestial, abyssal) and the special ones stay as they were. COSMETICS HAVE NO LEVEL GATES: the crates they come from drop by water, and that is their gate.
_milestones: Fishing's stat gains land at milestones (Kong, 2026-10-01): every 10 levels the catch zone grows 2 degrees and the perfect streak's ceiling takes one step, instead of a degree every 5 levels and a hair every level. The totals at 100 are the web's.
_skills: SKILLS (Kong, 2026-10-02): unlocked by Fishing level, free and permanent. They save time or show information; NONE touches catching (bites, rarity, zones, crates, size): that stays with gear. Quick sell sells the whole hold from anywhere at a share of today's Market price; the best owned rate applies. Recall: second_recall gives two recalls per period, quick_recall halves the period.

_market: THE MARKET DAY (Kong, 2026-10-02): prices change once a sea day (48 min), at sunrise (two thirds into the clock's cycle), each day with its own mood. The Advanced board needs Fishing 50 (levelGates.feature).
_achievements: ACHIEVEMENTS (Kong, 2026-10-02): badges pay nothing but their points; captain colours unlock at point milestones and come from nowhere else (not crates, not levels, not shops), save the four free starters. The milestones span the 236 points the port's badges can earn today (core/achievements.gd); stretch them as more systems are ported. The three dig badges belong to the treasure hunts now.

riddles.open_waters-4: A broken spar points out of me, west of home in the open water.
riddles.open_waters-5: Ships once rested here and none do now. Far west, in the open water.

riddles.abyss-3: I carry a light for nobody, south and a touch west in the Abyss.

_seaExpand: THE SEA WIDENED (Kong, 2026-10-02): everything past the Mainland's water (1,400 out) on the fishing side sits this much further out; the waters keep their widths. core/sea_scale.gd.
_fishBias: WHEN A FISH BITES BEST (Kong, 2026-10-02): while a condition holds where the line goes in, these species are nudged up among fish of their own rarity (+25%, +40% in a Tempest); never the odds of a rarer fish, never pay. No Fair Wind (Kong). core/fish_bias.gd.
_crewPort: THE CREW HALL (Kong, 2026-10-02): a fresh free board every SEA DAY (48 minutes), at sunrise (Kong: 'crew should refresh based on in-game days'); the hall reads Fishing where the web reads Navigation until Navigation is earned in the port. core/crew.gd.

crewPort._pityAfter: BAD-LUCK PROTECTION (Kong, 2026-10-10; a default Kong may tune): profile crew_pity counts posted notices in a row whose board had no Epic or better (any notice; the free board at sunrise does not count). Once it stands at pityAfter, the next posted board is sure of an Epic or better: if none rolled, one face is rolled again among that notice's own Epic and Legendary odds. 9: the tenth post at the latest.
crewPort._notices: NOTICES (Kong, 2026-10-02). Per face, three faces a board. The free board is the Tavern Notice: an Epic on 5% of boards, never a Legendary. A Harbor Bill: Epic on 15% of boards, a Legendary on 1 in 100. A Captain's Proclamation: Epic on 20%, a Legendary on about 1 in 34. Drops: Ship's Letter and Torn Map caskets 25% a Bill; Last Will caskets always a Bill and 10% a Proclamation; gold and diamond crates 3% a Bill; ancient crates 5% a Bill and 1% a Proclamation.

_finnJobs: THE LONG CAST'S PORT-ONLY JOBS (Kong, 2026-10-03: new job types). Each slots into Finn's ladder after the web job named in `after`; ids p1-p8 are never renumbered. Types: catch_species (the fish he describes, in the Log's words with its name veiled; measured off the lifetime log), catch_condition (cond: golden, storm, night or fog, at the cast spot, in the zone), catch_hotspot (spot: shoal, trench or flotsam), catch_trophy (a trophy-size fish in the zone). The last three are measured off profile.finn_tally, which the port bumps on every catch (Finn.on_catch); never under parity.

portJobs.done: That is the one. You knew it from a few words, which means you have been paying attention.

_casino: THE DEN IN THE PORT (Kong, 2026-10-02, SETTLED). Fish Slots is a gentle money sink: the Catfish Jackpot is a FIXED 300x the bet on three catfish (main reels or the bonus round), no shared pot and nothing fed into it; catfish weight 9 to 8 (about 1 spin in 1,895); triples sardine 3 / marlin 10 / great white 25 / whale 50; pairs marlin 1.25 / great white 2.5 / whale 4 / catfish 2; the bonus round (three hooks, Jellyfish wild, wins x1.5) and the two-hook refund stay. Exact enumeration: about 90% back (89.6% at 10 chips to 90.1% at 100 and up, pairs rounded down). The daily buy-in cap follows Fishing level alone: 1,000, +1,000 at 10, 20, 30 and 40, 7,500 at 70, 10,000 at 100. Roulette opens at Fishing 10 and Blackjack at 20 (levelGates.feature). No Crown & Anchor.
_skinVouchers: SKIN VOUCHERS (Kong, 2026-10-03, SETTLED, second shape): two kinds, found like crates and hard to get. Each rolls the skin's tier (rare, epic, legendary) by its weights over the tiers with a skin left; a Legendary crew's chase skins are in the legendary roll, each counting chaseWeight (0.75) to a plain skin's 1, so about 1 legendary roll in 5 is a chase skin (Kong: slightly harder to roll a chase once you roll a legendary) (a tier owned in full drops out, the rest keep their shares), then a skin in that tier at random; it can land on a crew not signed yet (it waits in the Trunk); worn at once if that crew is aboard and wears nothing. drops: chance per crate opened and per casket, by tier. The Parlor gives one Captain's Voucher, at Parlor Legend (parlorCapstone); its other ranks are titles. Every skin owned: allOwnedPays doubloons. Rough rates, ASSUMING about 45 crates and 8 caskets a month for a regular player (150 casts an hour, an hour a day): about one Bosun's Voucher a month in the middle waters, about five Captain's a year fishing the deepest. core/skins.gd.

_battle: THE BATTLE ENGINE (Kong, 2026-10-03, core/battle.gd): one engine for every fight, solo a party of one. Every captain keeps their OWN ship, HP, crew and balls; a sunk ship is out on its own. PARTY SCALING (tested on Pete's raid, a fair bot, 300 runs a size: 38% / 41% / 63% / 73% won): the ENEMY's HP times enemyHpMult by how many captains start the fight; an ordinary attack is shots[n-1] aimed shots, each at a ship it picks as it fires (hidden; focus: it may pick the same ship twice). BROADSIDES (Kong, 2026-10-03: "certain enemies should be able to hit all players at once, and bosses all have that ability for some of their hits"): every boss's volleys and ultimates, and the volleys of the enemies in broadside.enemyVolleys, hit EVERY ship at once, each rolling its own dodge. CROSSFIRE (Kong, 2026-10-03: skill based): when two or more ships land a CRITICAL on their own aim bar in the same round, each of those shots is multiplied by 1 + crossfire.pct for every crit past the first (two: x1.25, four: x1.75); a hit turned crit by gear does not count. In a field of several enemies, the crits must land on the SAME enemy (Kong: focus fire is the skill). TIERS (Kong, 2026-10-03): Co-op and Co-op Challenge, two or more captains (Challenge once every captain in the line has cleared that raid on Co-op). Several enemies at once, 1 to 4: an ordinary fight fields the party's size (sometimes one fewer; on Challenge sometimes one more), the fight's own enemy leading and escorts from the raid's crew; the boss comes with escorts. No party HP scaling on a field (more ships instead), except the boss (x bossHp of the party scale). Each enemy's ordinary attack is one aimed shot (a boss keeps a smaller volley of them). Pay: coin and XP times the tier's, escorts at escortPay of their kill; the crate rolls 1 + extraRolls times with rarities x rarityMult. (Kong, 2026-10-03: no pennants.) A tier's first clear is stamped on the screen, and each tier beaten shows as a gold seal on the entry screen and under the raid's ship. STATUSES EARLIER (Kong, 2026-10-03: "introduced earlier than it is today"; the web is frozen, the port's raids are its own): enemyMods gives the early raids' hands a status special each, IN PLACE OF ONE OF THEIR DODGES (never a reload: that starved their shot, turned a volley the pattern promised into a reload and broke the rhythm players read; nor added as an extra turn: a free breather made the raid easier than charted), one new idea a raid: Pete Feeble and Fortify, Krust Weaken, Slowed and Fortify, the Cartographer BLINDED, the Tollmaster NARROWED and Weaken, the Coffers Marked and Enrage, the Quartermaster Silence. ROLES (co-op fields only): each escort one of roles.list; every few of its turns it spends the turn on its role, instantly: a Shieldwright shields its most hurt ally, a Sawbones heals one, a Hexer blinds or narrows a captain, a Rallier enrages the whole line; a Breakwater (passive) sometimes takes a shot meant for an ally.

battle._gauntlet: A GAUNTLET PARTY'S FIELD (Kong, 2026-10-03: multiple ships for enemies just like in raids). Alone, a dive is the web's one ship a depth. Two to four captains meet the party's size in ships (sometimes one fewer, now and then one more, 1 to 4): the lead at leadHp of the depth's curve, escorts (mobs of the same depth, each with its own elite roll and a co-op role) at escortHp; a boss at bossHp times the party's HP table, with escorts. Damage times dmgMult. Each escort sunk adds half a mob's pot.
battle._reactions: REACTIONS (Kong, 2026-10-03: hidden Magicka-style combos, "discoverable Easter eggs for coop"; co-op gauntlets only). When two elements on one enemy ship came from DIFFERENT captains (fire, ice, corrode, weaken, feeble, marked, Kraken coils; or a Volley or Mega into one), they react. At most one reaction per ship per round; damage scales off the hit, never the ship's hull. Hidden in the Codex until a crew sets one off (gauntlet_reactions_seen), with a count of how many are left.
battle._packs: CO-OP PACKS (Kong, 2026-10-03: enemy groups "fair yet more interesting", mixed packs in middle-late runs): a co-op field's escorts come as one fleet's crew sized by a threat budget (packs.budget by party size, +/- spread, bossCut fewer under a boss, deepBonus deeper), each ship costing packs.cost by its kind, +roleCost for a role, +eliteCost for an elite affix. Roles from the fleet's own list (at most one support and one other per pack; support ships sail at supportHp). From mixFrom a pack may draw from two fleets (mixChance). From comboFrom one named COMBO may join a role ship and a partner (combos; never on an elite-affix ship); it breaks when either half sinks. Shown on the enemy's card. Solo fights have no escorts and are untouched.
battle._bonds: BOND POWERS (Kong, 2026-10-03: co-op gauntlets need their own things; "specialize into different helper class builds ... support roles or healer or tank roles while others choose more classic damage"; single-player balance untouched). Dealt ONLY on a co-op draft table: at most one per spread, on rare-like odds (chance bondChance), each card the next tier for whoever takes it; role tags tank, healer, support, gunner. Their effects (kinds bond*) run only when a captain holds one, so solo fights roll exactly as before. Crew synergies: a synergy whose two powers are held by two different captains may come up at the table (chance crewSynChance); either of the two may take it with their pick, and both get it at the lower of their tiers. Rewards: the Fleet Chest (+fleetPerCaptain to a co-op bank's doubloons for each captain afloat past the first) and skin vouchers by depth (vouchers, a full crew of four banking at fullCrewDepth rolls twice).

stories: There were six of them, they say. Big as ships and older than ships. Five accounted for.
My father worked the Deep forty years and never went past it. Said the water changes temper out there.
Ask about the Finndicate in a tavern and watch who leaves.
Someone's been buying up charts. All of them. Paying stupid money and asking no questions.
The carvings on those stones aren't writing. I've shown them to people who'd know.
A man I knew went out past the Abyss on a bet. Came back. Wouldn't fish again.
You'll hear it said the deep ones are dead. Landed isn't dead.
Whatever counts to six down there, don't answer it.

chapter_2_class.flavor: Four Finndicate captains on the seabed and the Gullet drained dry. Time to decide what your name stands for where the coin sleeps.

gullet_raid.bridge: Spet goes down and the Gullet drains dry. Four Finndicate captains on the seabed, a set of books nobody was ever meant to audit, and past here the cold water answers to a don even Spet would not name.

scene.text: Past the strait, someone has made a counter out of a wrecked hull and a barrel, and is waiting behind it.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: Two things on the barrel, captain. You take one.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: It's free. Don't ask why. And I don't repeat myself.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: Everyone who crosses that strait ends up at my counter sooner or later. You'll be back.

quartermaster.bridge: The Quartermaster gives away more than he lets on. The cold water ahead answers to one captain, and the wax on Pete's letter finally has a name behind it.

scene.text: The Coffers. Seems like a place for the Finndicate elite. Even the air smells rich.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: It's a whole exchange out here. Everything must get traded at the harbor.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: So all the funds get tracked and then divvied up here?

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Seems like it. I feel like we're on a fast track to the real inner workings of the Finndicate now.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Looks like our reputation hasn't caught up to us yet... but before long they'll know of what we did.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: Oh I know what you've all done.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Who...!

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: At ease, captains. Laz. I'm here looking to infiltrate Finndicate operations. They took down my family business.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: I've worked peacefully for years as a retired captain. They started pillaging our businesses for no reason. I managed to track down one of their merchant ships and have been following ever since.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: I came here once before to ask them why. They wrote me into the books as a debt, closed the account, and left me in this water. I'm the one entry they got wrong.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: Not to sound creepy. But they've mentioned a motley crew going around taking down pieces of their operation one at a time. Their description... was accurate.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: ...And we just trust this?

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: We did for you.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: Trust me or not, having eavesdropped on their merchant ships, I know my way around the harbor a bit now. I'm sure I'd be a valuable resource for your team.
Laz joins the party. He is now recruitable from the Crew Hall.
Three laborious days going through everything in Krust's hold... crate by crate by crate. Nothing of value was getting sent out. But there is a pattern.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Instruments. Sounding lines... oil, glass. What is the purpose of all of this?

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: There's something specific they're after.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: Where is this all going to?

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: A chartmaker.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Who are you?

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: Dole. I've dabbled in charting myself. This is all survey gear, friends. I've been trying to find out who's been stealing my goods and where it's all gone.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: A chartmaker? Shouldn't the Finndicate know their way around by now?

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: Around the known parts, yes. But those aren't the parts a chartmaker gets paid for.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: You know who they're paying then?

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: I had a hunch. But I've confirmed it now that you all took down Krust. I was able to match the heading to where the shipments would go to.
Dole sets a map down facing you.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: I'd be happy to help out. The northern seas aren't for the blind.
Dole joins the party. He is now recruitable from the Crew Hall.
You find Pete's strongbox. But there's no treasure inside. Just... paperwork?
Cut sheets. Courier routes. Years of accounting.
One word is stamped on every page: *the Finndicate*.
A note in Pete's own scrawl is pinned inside the lid: *You think I keep the coin? Not a doubloon stays with me.*

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Hmm... Pete was nothing but a pawn. He works for someone else. No wonder he plundered so much and had so little to show for it.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: The Finndicate. I've heard the name. They control the outer seas... but they're mostly involved in commercial business. Why would Pete involve himself...
The pages say the same thing over and over again. Funds needed for purchases, but no reason behind them.
Under the ledgers there is a sealed letter. No name, but two initials: *C.K.*
The route is mostly burned away, but you make out a path out past the Bilge Strait.
Whoever C.K. is, the Finndicate trusts him with the cargo. Seems like many small captains like Barnacle Pete are shipping their plunder to him.
You notice that someone's been trailing you for a while now... you've felt their presence ever since you came into Pete's quarters.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: Hmm... the Bilge Strait huh? Most captains wouldn't sail through there just based on a hunch. Good thing neither of us is the average captain.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: Name's Mako. Common enemy means we're partners. I've been trying to lock down Pete for a while now. Seems like we had a common goal. Muster a crew and my name's on the table.
Mako joins the party. He is now recruitable from the Crew Hall.

detail.description: Six ship battles this time, same old corsair at the end, but every hull he's put back on the water is a step harder than the last. The Raiders hit cleaner, the Marksman aims truer, and Pete fights like a captain who's finally noticed you're still here. Crack his crate this time and the contraband runs richer for it.

one_last_ride_challenge.flavor: The water still remembers the shape of him. Go again, with none of the mercy.

detail.description: Five phases, six stolen giants, and a chain you cannot afford to drop. Everything he does hits harder and his own rhythm is tighter, so the Perfect Streak stops being a reward and starts being the requirement.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Now that you've got your ship and a crew, let's take care of some business. It's been far too long since someone put a stop to Barnacle Pete.
He's robbed the weak and poor for years. All up and down this coast.
Little crew. Fishing folk. The odd unlucky angler. Anyone too small to swing back.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: And here's the part that doesn't make sense. Pete steals so much but never has anything to show for it.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: I think it's time we do something about it. We've scouted him out just further down the waters.

scene.speaker: Barnacle Pete
scene.text: Heard there's some new folk in town to plunder.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Charming, isn't he? Let's go shake him up and see what he's up to.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Remember, if you don't feel like you're ready, go back and make sure you get some stronger crew aboard!

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Can always learn the hard way. Onward!
All this travel just for two letters: C.K.
Now we know.
*Captain Krust*.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Krust. He's in charge of moving the Finndicate's freight.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: The Finndicate must trust him. He must know he's taking in stolen goods.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: Smarter than Pete for sure.
Krust has been moving commercial goods for ages. But these days, it looks like he's funneling more stolen cargo than actual goods.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: His activities are suspicious.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Definitely. Someone is behind all of this... but we'll have to get through Krust to see what's going on.
Krust's goals are uncertain. But it'll certainly be harder to get through to Krust than Pete.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: Ready your guns, captain. His crew spotted us!

chapter_3_class.flavor: The Coffers in ruins, the Quartermaster under, and his tracker at the bottom of the sea. Time to set what your colors mean before the deepest water.

chapter_4_augment.flavor: The Don kept a shipwright the way other captains keep a surgeon. He works for you now. One last refit, bolted to your deck for good.

detail.description:
The Don's own shipwright owes you his freedom, and he pays it in iron. He can cut your deck for one more RAID-ITEM MOUNT: an extra piece of gear working every fight, on every raid from here on.

It costs a fortune. Take his plans to your shipwrights in Manage Ship when you are ready to pay for it.
detail.summary: The Don's shipwright owes you his freedom and pays it in iron: an extra RAID-ITEM MOUNT cut into your deck for a fortune, one more piece of gear working every fight. Buy it in Manage Ship.

the_throne_challenge.flavor: The court reconvenes, and this time the Don skips the pleasantries.

the_throne.flavor: The court rides at anchor and the Don sits still at the center of it, done talking. Every hull here carries a trick you haven't been hit with yet. And the Don carries all of them.
the_throne.bridge: The court is drowned and the Don with it. The biggest name in the sea, finally answered for. Or so it seems.

detail.description: The don's own court, and every hull in it fights with a new kind of dirty. Watch their cannonball pips: a FULL, glowing battery means an ULTIMATE is primed. Burn their charges down, shield, or brace before it empties into you. And their specials strike your AIM BAR itself: false gold you must not lock, plated locks that take two taps, squalls that gust your needle mid-sweep. Don Finleone waits at the center, and he doesn't fight to win. He fights for control.

spoils_of_the_hand.label: What Finn Left
spoils_of_the_hand.flavor: Everything the Finndicate took went back. These two were his own, and nobody else has a use for them.
spoils_of_the_hand.bridge: One is a reel. One is a mount. Both were Finn's, and only one fits aboard today.

detail.description:
He left two things behind worth taking, and they answer to the two halves of your life out here.

THE DEEP REEL opens a SECOND special slot on your fishing rig, and only The Primeval Eye will seat in it.

THE SIXTH MOUNT frames one more raid item onto your hull, and only The Primeval Maw will mount there.

Neither tool is in your hold yet. This opens the berth. The water still has to give the piece up.

Take one now. The other keeps, and it keeps expensive.

the_long_quiet.bridge: Finn is gone, the giants are home, and what the Finndicate took is going back to those it was taken from.

detail.description:
Finn is gone, and the six he took have gone back down where you found them.

What the Finndicate stole is still out there, and the crew mean to give it back.
detail.summary: Finn is gone and the Finndicate with him. The crew took what it had stolen and gave it back, then each went their own way.

scene.text: The last shot lands, and the sea is still.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: ...impossible.
Finn is defeated, yet still stands on his last remaining breath.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: How could you...possibly defeat me?
The light that was running under his skin turns and fades.
The power of the ancients leaves him. One by one, they withdraw from him.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: I had it all. I finally got what I wanted...

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: A lifetime. I gave a whole lifetime for this.
He looks at you the way he did before...when he was just a mere angler.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: ...you were never supposed to defeat me. To stop me.
What is left of him goes up rather than down, gray and weightless, and the wind takes it apart before it clears the mast.
And then the water is quiet, and there is a small boat sitting on it.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: Heh.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: Would you look at that. All of it gone. Like a vapor. I had it all...
Finn is back to how he was.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: I was once just like you...

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: Just a humble fisher...
He is starting to fade away.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: Me and you are nearly the same...just a little bit of power...that's all it took...and I spent my life chasing it...all for nothing...
No one says a word.
The sea hangs for a second, and then Finn disappears, swallowed into the deep.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: ...he's gone.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: It's over...

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: He was just a regular like any of us...corrupted by power.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: At the end of the day, it could be any of us if we're not careful.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: That's why we're anchored by one another. He never had a crew...he just had himself.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: That's why you never sail alone.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: I can't believe all this destruction was caused by one sailor's greed.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: It would've gotten worse before it got better, had we not come in to stop it.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: He left storehouses of treasures. All that the Finndicate took from others.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: As much as I want the fastest ship on the sea to myself...if there's anything I've learned, it's that chasing after treasure won't make you happier.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: We give back to those he's taken from. And rebuild what was destroyed.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: That's fitting for our one last ride.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: One last ride.
The crew takes in all the treasure that they can store. But not for themselves.
To rebuild a community destroyed by greed, by giving back to those who need it most.
Epilogue.
Mira rebuilds her crew. Goes back to the families of her fallen crew and gets them back on their feet.
Laz raises a new community and trains a new generation of sailors.
Dole goes back to chartmaking, and makes it his mission to map the entire sea and make it free for all sailors.
Mako goes back to bounty hunting, not for his own personal gain, but to live out his own passion.
And Doby and Kat go back to living the simple life. Dreams of power and prosperity fade away as they re-learn the joy of just sailing the seas.

one_last_ride.label: One Last Ride
one_last_ride.flavor: No more captains between you. Just the water, and the angler who's been reeling you in the whole time.

detail.description: One last ride, captain. Everything the Finndicate ever took comes down to this water.
detail.summary: The last fight. Read The Finndicate Lives On first.

the_hand_that_sharpens.label: The Finndicate Lives On
the_hand_that_sharpens.flavor: Six giants came up out of the Ancient Deep on your line, and every one of them went somewhere. You never once asked where. The Don swore the Finndicate lives on. He was right.

detail.summary: What the six giants were really for. Opens once all six Ancient Deep giants are caught.

scene.text: The sixth giant is caught. The sea has been quiet ever since.
Then a heading comes. It's a small boat... with someone sitting in the stern and a line in the water. Whoever it is does not turn around when you come alongside.

scene.speaker: The Angler
scene.text: Took you long enough, captain. I almost ran out of patience. And you know how patient fishers are. Thank you for doing my dirty work. Don Finleone failed me. Even with all the resources I gave him. No one could get me what I actually wanted. No one had the capabilities to do so...until you.
You know that voice. You can't really remember...but you definitely recognize it.
He turns around.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: Surprised? Heh.
Finn!
The one you first met in the southern shores.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Finn?! You were behind all of this?

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: But you're... you're just a fisher. You sit on a dock all day.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: How is this possible? You orchestrated all of it? You're behind...everything?

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: The Don was the perfect alibi. How could anyone think of me? Like you said, I am just a fisher after all.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: But...the Finndicate...how were you managing everything?

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: My campaign in the northern seas was one to control all trade. To funnel all resources to boost my own capabilities. For my own goal. I am Finn. The Finndicate runs through me.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Finn...he's the "F" in the letters. Don Finleone was never the one...

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: I knew I had to track you all as soon as you settled into the seas. Watching your growth as a fisher...as a navigator...I knew you had the ultimate potential to get me what I wanted.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: And now you have them. You proved me right. You caught the six ancients...the legendary creatures that are known to give you almost unlimited power. Power that you have no idea how to use.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: I rerouted every shipment. Every resource. Every plunder. To give me the tools, the capabilities, to find and catch these ancients. But I knew that you would be led right to them instead. I just had to keep tabs on you. And make sure you never escaped my sight.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: I deserve to rule these seas. I built an empire. I've tried so hard, yet the ancients never showed up for me. But when I saw you...the potential you had from the first day.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: You kept fishing...growing in your skill daily. Working through the deepest waters until you found the ancients and caught each one.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: You impressed me, captain. Truly.
It is the first nice thing he has said, and somehow it doesn't make you feel any better.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: I let you sail freely. Every door you kicked down, I left unlocked. You cleared out my own house and called it a campaign, and you got stronger every time you did it.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Captain...what do we do...

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: You have the very ones I need now...all these years. Patiently waiting. Waiting for the one who was worthy.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Captain...
He points over to your ship.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: I feel their energy.
He motions for them to come out from your own ship's hold.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: How is he...??
One by one their essence is drawn out in a ring around him.
And one by one...their power starts feeding into Finn.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: He's...absorbing them?
The sea flattens. It's eerily quiet.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: The hold. Captain, the hold is empty. They're gone.
What comes down on the water afterward is only the shape.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: Finally.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: A lifetime of waiting. Finally. The power I have been longing for.
Finn crackles with energy as he grows larger.
Light opens along him in cracks.
The morning goes white, and then it goes dark from him outward.
The old angler is gone. The new one is...

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: What is...happening...?

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Who is he becoming...?

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: This can't be good. And we thought the Don was the worst of our issues.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: I've never seen anything like this before...

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: Ah. There it is.
The water pulls back from the boat. Even the deep is giving him room.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: This power...

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: Thank you...I really couldn't have done it without you. You really helped me become my true potential.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: This isn't good captain...

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: One last ride, then. You and me. Join me. We can rule together. I do owe you for the hard work that you did after all.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: I'd rather die than join you.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: You have lied and cheated and stolen from too many. No one in their right mind would want to join you.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: I almost feel bad. It almost felt like we were friends. All the favors you did for me all this time. I thought we had a connection.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: Very well. We'll have one last ride either way. Shame you won't be joining me any more.
It has all led up to this. The real head of the Finndicate. Finn himself. It's going to be a bumpy ride.

chapter_4_close.flavor: The Don goes down, but not before promising the Finndicate lives on. Then something stirs out past the wreck, and the crew takes the longest watch together.
chapter_4_close.bridge: The Don is on the seabed and the crew is whole. Surely the calm means the journey's over.

detail.description: Don Finleone is on the seabed. With his last breath he swears the Finndicate lives on, and out past the wreck something watches the ruin you made, then sinks out of sight. Was he bluffing? Tonight the crew takes the longest watch together and drinks to peace in the northern seas.
detail.summary: Don Finleone went down swearing the Finndicate lives on. Something watched from past the wreck, then sank. The crew took the longest watch together, sure the journey was over.

scene.text: The megalodon has met his fate. Finally.
But he has breath for a few more words.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Let him talk...

scene.speaker: Don Finleone
scene.text: You think you've won...you think the Finndicate falls with me. No...the Finndicate lives on...
The Don sinks for the first and last time. Generations of drowned debts sink to the bottom with him.
Then, out past the wreck, where the Don's water spills over into the true deep, the black surface stirs. Another shark...no...another sailor tracking the consequences of your actions?
Was the Don bluffing when he said the Finndicate lives on? Surely not...who could be above Don Finleone, the leader of the Finndicate?

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Captain. Tell me you saw that too...
The court settles to the seabed, and for the first time in a very long time, there is nothing ahead to point at. So the crew takes the longest watch of all. Together.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: We've defeated the Finndicate...but I feel like I didn't get all the answers I wanted.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Sometimes you have to create the answers yourself. And for us, we've accomplished what we came here for.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: The biggest bounty of the sea...couldn't have done it without you lot.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: Going back to chartmaking seems rather dull after all this, but I sure have learned a lot more of what I want to chart.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: The drowned can finally rest. The Don finally gets what he deserves.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Here's to an era of peace in the northern seas.
Tonight the crew is whole, the grog is cold, and the whole sea knows your name. The Don is taken care of. The Finndicate, eradicated. Surely the calm signals the end of the journey.

within_hail.flavor: The aisle of guns opens onto the throne, and for the first time the Don speaks. He says the Finndicate takes for one reason: control.
within_hail.bridge: The Don has said his piece: control, and he calls it order. There is nothing left between you and him.

detail.description: The aisle opens onto the throne, and the Don finally speaks. He calls the Finndicate a business, then admits what it's really after: control. Order for the seas, he says, paid for by the weak. Then he tells you to brace yourself.
detail.summary: Within hail of the throne, the Don spoke: the Finndicate takes from the weak for control, and he calls it order. Then he told you to brace yourself.

scene.text: The court holds its fire and its formation, every gun tracking you in, and the lit flagship at the end grows from a lantern to a leviathan.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: It's the Don...

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: He's bigger than I thought...

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Hold your ground. We didn't get all the way to him for nothing.
Close enough to hail now, and the Don, who has not stirred this entire time, finally lifts his head and regards you the way you would look at a coin you have already spent.

scene.speaker: Don Finleone
scene.text: I'm almost impressed, little captain. You've made a fool of many a captain getting here.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Save your compliments, Don.

scene.speaker: Don Finleone
scene.text: That's no way to greet a superior, is it?

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: We'll give you one chance to tell us everything. What is the Finndicate up to? Nothing you're doing makes sense.

scene.speaker: Don Finleone
scene.text: What about it doesn't make sense? I'm accumulating resources for our business.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: There's no business going on here. You're disguising your business for some ulterior motive. Why in the seas would you need to raid every resource? There's shipments unrelated to your business coming through your ledgers.

scene.speaker: Don Finleone
scene.text: The Finndicate is bigger than you think...you don't know what you're up against. Resources are merely used to advance us all. We believe that we use resources for the greatest purpose.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: And what's that purpose?

scene.speaker: Don Finleone
scene.text: Control.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: No one wants the Finndicate to have control.

scene.speaker: Don Finleone
scene.text: Plenty do. We're merely trying to make the seas safer. Without any sort of order...you'll see how everyone suffers as a result. We take from the weak because they wouldn't have survived anyway.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: If this is the best you've got, I'm afraid your days are numbered.

scene.speaker: Don Finleone
scene.text: My days have always been numbered. But you won't be part of that reason. Brace yourself, little captain.

the_last_muster.flavor: Before the throne, Kat lines everyone up one last time. The Don's court fires as one, and nobody faces it short a hand.
the_last_muster.bridge: Kat's satisfied. Nothing stands between you and the throne now but open water.

detail.description:
Kat checks the crew one last time before the throne.

What waits there answers to nothing but the right hand at the right moment: a brace or a shield when the whole court fires as one, a mender when the Don's jaws find your hull, and someone who can jam or blast him out of a dive.

To pass: 5 crew aboard, every hand Level 65 or higher, someone who can Brace or Shield, someone who can Heal, and someone who can Snare or fire a Heavy Salvo.

This is the fight the Sixth Berth was built for. Field your whole crew.
detail.summary: Kat checked every hand one last time, and the crew came up ready for the throne.

scene.text: The court parts, but the aisle to the throne is long, and every gun in it is tracking you.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: One more time, everyone. Line up.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: Again? We just did this.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: That was before Sal. Show me those fins.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: The Don doesn't fight alone. When the court fires, they fire together.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: Then someone has to cover the ship, someone has to patch us up, and someone has to stop him when he dives.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: Every hand we've got, then.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Every hand we've got. Captain, your crew.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Hat off again?

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Hat off.

the_drowned_court.flavor: The gates open on the Don's own black water, and his court rides at anchor around one lit flagship: six shark-captains, his own flesh and blood.
the_drowned_court.bridge: The Closer has said his piece and slid back into the ring. The aisle to the Don's throne stands open.

detail.description: The Don's court rides at anchor around his lit flagship: six shark-captains, his own flesh and blood and his highest-ranking officers. One of them, the Closer, comes out to meet you, and he says the Finndicate isn't what you think it is. Then the court parts, and the aisle to the throne opens.
detail.summary: Past the gates, the Don's court rode at anchor around his flagship. The Closer came out to meet you and claimed the Finndicate borrows for a greater good. Nobody bought it.

scene.text: You slip into the Don's own black water. No horns. No warning shot. Just the pressure of the deep and one lit flagship far ahead, ringed by its court.
Six hulls ride at anchor around it, arrayed like courtiers around a throne. The Don does not play around.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Here we are...the court of the Don himself.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: I can't tell if I'm happy to be here or not.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: You should never be happy when you're surrounded by sharks.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: You're a shark, Mako.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: I'm one of the good ones...a rare breed. Most are ruthless, raised like that from birth.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: You know anything about his little armada here?

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: As you saw with Sal, only his highest ranking officers get to be this close to him. Sal was his right hand, but he wasn't a shark. These sharks are his own flesh and blood.
One hull peels from the ring, all cold precision, and stops across your bow. Close enough to read the old scars crossing his plating like a ledger of every captain he has closed.

scene.speaker: The Closer
scene.text: The Don sends his regards.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Let's cut to the chase here...the Don has been terrorizing the northern seas for none other than his own selfish gain. Anyone getting in our way is going to be taken care of.

scene.speaker: The Closer
scene.text: I don't think you know who you're dealing with, little captain.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: I think we all know who we're dealing with. We've been hunting you down for an eternity, and we're finally ready to end your Finndicate operations.

scene.speaker: The Closer
scene.text: You know nothing about the Finndicate.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: What is there to know? You steal and plunder for your own personal gain. Preying on the weak will only get you so far.

scene.speaker: The Closer
scene.text: The Finndicate doesn't prey on the weak. We borrow resources for a greater good. How easy it is to only hear one side of the story.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: You destroyed my crew for no reason other than for your selfish gain.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: As with mine. I can't think of any defendable reason for the actions of the Finndicate.

scene.speaker: The Closer
scene.text: And this is why they say sharks have the biggest brains. Your tiny minds can't comprehend what we're trying to do.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: Sharks don't have the biggest brains...

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: Hey...

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: And it doesn't take anyone with a big brain to figure out that the Don just wants more power. And that ends right here.

scene.speaker: The Closer
scene.text: Very well. The Don will get what he wants, either way.
The Closer holds a moment longer, as if offering you the chance to turn.

crooked_ledger.label: The Don's Orders
crooked_ledger.flavor: Sal's sea chest comes up out of the wreck, full of the Don's orders. Every job Sal ever ran for him is in there. One last lock, and then the Don's throne.
crooked_ledger.bridge: Sal's orders are read, Mira's crew among them, signed by the Don. One last lock, and then the Don's throne.

detail.description: Sal kept every order the Don ever gave him: every ship sunk, every harbor taken, Mira's crew among them. Most are in the Don's hand. The oldest aren't. Nothing between you and the throne now but one last lock.
detail.summary: Sal's sea chest held every order the Don ever gave him, Mira's crew among them. The oldest were signed with a single F. One last lock stands between you and the throne.

scene.text: Sal's hull breaks open, and his sea chest floats up out of the wreck.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Heavy...even for a bodyguard.
Inside: orders. Hundreds of them, folded and sealed. Every job Sal ever ran for the Don.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: Sink this merchant. Take that harbor. Clear this crew. He kept every single one.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: ...this one's mine. My crew. My ship. Signed by the Don himself.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: I'm sorry, Mira.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Don't be. Now I've seen it in his own hand.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: Hmm. Not all of these are in the Don's hand.
The oldest orders are written differently. Each one signed with a single letter, looped small at the bottom: F.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: F for Finleone?

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: Yeah...makes sense. Wonder why he goes by Don and then F at other times. Like pick a name and stick with it.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Yeah, that's interesting.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Sal wasn't easy, I'll give you that. But let's get ready to take down the Don once and for all.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: I still have so many questions...

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: We all do. Let's get the answers we've been waiting for.

sixth_berth.flavor: The Don's bodyguard never sailed short-handed. He came apart along the grain, the way he tore everything else apart, and his hull showed you its bones on the way down. Six berths framed into a deck that had no business carrying more than five. Nobody does that by accident.

the_blockade.flavor: The Don's guard line, and the one who holds it: Sal Brackwater, the Don's bodyguard. Every hull rides behind a cold-light barrier, every magazine runs four deep, and his line fights dirtier than any market ever did.
the_blockade.bridge: The Don's bodyguard goes under, and for the first time nothing stands between you and the Don.

detail.description:
The don's escort fleet, and it does not fight like anything you have met.

Every hull rides behind a barrier, so your opening shots buy nothing but broken plating. Their magazines run four deep, and a ship that has been firing all round is never as empty as you would like. And they fight dirty: nets for your rudder, chain-shot for your guns, cracker rounds for your seams, and a gag order for your crew.

At the center of the line, Sal Brackwater waits.

thing_on_the_bar.label: The Don's Bodyguard
thing_on_the_bar.flavor: A line of guard ships sits across the flat water, lanterns out. In the middle, one low, dark hull that hasn't moved since you spotted it.
thing_on_the_bar.bridge: The Don's bodyguard is out on the water, and he's waiting for you.

detail.description: The Don's own guard line, and at its center his bodyguard, Sal Brackwater. He has never failed the Don's orders, and the Don has sent him out to deal with you first.
detail.summary: The Don sent his bodyguard, Sal Brackwater, to deal with you first. Mira knows him: he's the one who took down her crew.

scene.text: The water ahead is flat. Too flat. A line of hulls sits across it, lanterns out.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: That's no merchant line. Those are...

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Guards. Look at the ship in the middle.
A low, dark hull sits at the center of the line. It hasn't moved since you spotted it.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: I know who that is.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Who?

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Sal Brackwater. You could say he's the Don's bodyguard. He's never been more than 3 fins away from the Don.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Then why is he all the way out here?

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: The Don probably knows we're coming. He sent his "bodyguard" to deal with us first.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: A crocodile. Great. I've always wanted to wrestle one.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Sal took down my crew. On the Don's orders. As much as I hate him, he's not a captain to take lightly.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: We've taken down our fair share at this point, Mira.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Sal's a different beast. You took down some of the Don's captains, but there's no one he trusts more to take care of business than Sal. He has never failed the Don's orders.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Well time to make some history.
Across the flat water, the low hull still hasn't moved. But you're sure now: it's watching you.

throne_locks.bridge: The hold is stowed tight and the guns are fed. Ahead: the blockade, and the Don's enforcer who runs it.

blockade_muster.flavor: Before the blockade, Kat lines everyone up on deck. Nobody sails into the Don's water hurt, green, or without a way to stop what's coming.
blockade_muster.bridge: Kat's satisfied. Everyone's fit, and the crew can take a hit. Time to face the blockade.

detail.description:
Kat checks the whole crew before you sail on: who's fit, who's ready, and who can actually do something when the shooting starts.

What's past this point can't be out-shot. Sal Brackwater will take your hull in his teeth and roll, and the ONLY thing that stops it is a crew ability. Not a dodge. Not a good shot. A crew member who can get between you and the blow.

To pass: 5 crew aboard, every hand Level 60 or higher, someone who can Brace or Shield, and someone who can Heal.
detail.summary: Kat checked every hand before the blockade and the crew came up ready.

scene.text: Before the blockade, Kat lines everyone up on deck.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Alright, everyone. Nobody's sailing into the Don's water hurt. Show me those fins.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: I'm fine. A few scratches. They add character.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: They add infection. Next.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: I've checked the charts three times. Whatever's past here, we can't outrun it and we can't out-shoot it.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Sal Brackwater doesn't miss. He grabs your hull in his jaws and rolls. I've seen it.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: Then we need someone who can take that hit for the ship, and someone who can patch us up after.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Which is why nobody sails on until I've checked every one of you. Captain, your crew.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Do I have to take my hat off?

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Yes.

throne_heading.flavor: The Coffers burn behind you and the chart runs out. Past the last sounding lies the Don's own water, and you aren't the only one sailing it.
throne_heading.bridge: The heading is set for the Don's own water, and Mira sails with you. So does the Quartermaster's seized stock.

detail.description: Past the Coffers there's no more market and no more middlemen. The chart runs out here: this is the Don's own water, the deepest there is. And somebody else out here has a score to settle with him.
detail.summary: The heading is set past the last sounding on any chart. For the deepest water there is, and the don who rules it. The final chapter has begun.

scene.text: The Coffers burn low behind you, and the sea ahead simply runs out of chart...you're in the Don's quarters now.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: The seas are not friendly here...that's for sure.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Nothing is friendly at these depths.
You aren't the only one sailing in these waters though. A distant figure approaches.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: Show yourself!

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Hmm...friend or foe?

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Depends on who's asking.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: I curse the Don's name. He ruined our crew and stripped us of all our belongings. If you work for the Don, I'll have you answer for his atrocities.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: At ease...we're after the same captain.
Mira relaxes her guard.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Mira. I've been looking to sail into the Don's quarters but the waters haven't been kind to what little I have.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: If we have a common enemy, then join us.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Enemy is too light of a word, but I'm in for the cause.
She lets her sail settle in beside yours and joins the party.
Mira joins the party. She is now recruitable from the Crew Hall.

chapter_3_close.flavor: The Quartermaster's tracker goes over the side, and for the first time since the coast nobody knows where you are. The Coffers burn low and the crew takes a watch before the deepest water.
chapter_3_close.bridge: The tracker's gone, and you know who runs it all now: the Don, Finleone. Past the last of the Coffers' light, the sea drops toward the seat he rules from.

detail.description: The brass box under the Quartermaster's counter has been listening to your gear since the start. Over the side it goes. Now you know who runs the whole business: the Don, at the head of the Finndicate. The Coffers burn low and the crew takes a watch, with more questions than answers and a long way still to sail.
detail.summary: The Quartermaster's tracker went over the side, and nobody knows where you are anymore. The Don runs the Finndicate. The crew took a watch before the deepest water, with plenty of questions left.

scene.text: Under the Quartermaster's counter, the brass box is still humming. Every piece of your gear has been talking to it since the start.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Shall I, captain?
It goes over the side in pieces. For the first time since the coast, nobody knows where you are.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: Well now we know who runs this whole business.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: The Don.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: The head of the Finndicate. So many questions still...
The Coffers burn low, the Quartermaster's counter down to kindling, and for the first time since the harbor gate the deck goes quiet.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: At least we're no longer being tracked...from what I can tell.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: And I'm glad I got some form of vengeance at the very least.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Seems like these captains have just been puppets of the Don.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: If I had known how long this journey was going to be, I would've probably stayed at home charting.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: At least there's some light at the end now.
Past the last of the Coffers' light, the sea drops away toward the seat the Don rules from. But that is tomorrow's heading.
Tonight the crew is whole, one hand heavier still, and the grog is cold.

the_quartermaster.flavor: The Don's Quartermaster, behind his own guns. Everything you carry from his caches still answers to him, and he opens by switching one of them off.
the_quartermaster.bridge: The Quartermaster goes down behind his own counter. Under it sits the brass box every piece of your gear has been reporting to since the coast. It goes over the side in pieces, and your gear is yours again.

detail.description: The Quartermaster himself, behind his own guns. His tracker is in every piece he ever left you, and he uses it: one of your raid items is switched off for the whole fight. He fights all misdirection: he floods the bay with false flares to foul your aim, and slips live shells in among them that you'll regret swatting. Read the real targets, intercept the rest, then put him under, through his reserve deck and all, to spill the Cache's hold.

coffers_fleet.flavor: The Finndicate's coffers keep a war-fleet, and Admiral Ruse has never lost a hull. His gunners fly false colors on every shot, so you never know which gun is the one that's loaded.
coffers_fleet.bridge: Admiral Ruse's fleet is wreckage on the harbor floor, and the Finndicate's coffers lie open. Whatever their mission is, it's paid for in there.

detail.description: The Coffers' war-fleet and its admiral, Ruse, who has never lost a ship. His crews fight under false colors: decoy gun-bands strewn across your aim so you can't tell the live shot from the feint. The biggest hulls you've faced yet, and Ruse rises again when you think you've sunk him.

coffers_fleet_challenge.flavor: The same fleet, drilled harder and flying meaner colors. Admiral Ruse doesn't lose his wall twice.

coffers_strongbox.flavor: With Ruse's fleet on the harbor floor, the Coffers' counting-house is in a panic. Clerks are running, coin is everywhere, and a strongbox full of the day's take is still bolted to the floor. The guards are regrouping fast. Time for one grab.

scene.text: Ruse's flagship goes under, and the whole counting-house watches it go.
Clerks bolt. Coin scatters across the planks. Somewhere a bell starts ringing.
Bolted to the floor by the scales sits a strongbox, the lid still warm from the day's counting.
The Finndicate's guards are regrouping at the far doors. You've got time for one grab. Make it count.

coffers_strongbox.bridge: Strongbox settled one way or the other, you push deeper into the Coffers, toward the light-lock that bars the vault.

detail.description: Ruse is sunk and the Coffers' counting-house has gone to pieces: clerks running, coin underfoot, the guards regrouping at the doors. Bolted to the planks by the scales sits a strongbox fat with the day's take. You get one grab before the guards get back to you. Throw the bones on it: skim the loose till for safe coin, force the box for more, or powder-charge the whole safe for everything it holds, knowing a bad roll costs you.

coffers_vault_lens.flavor: The Coffers' vault answers to a lock of light: a sunbeam brought down through the roof by a row of mirrors, every one of them knocked crooked. Straighten them and the vault opens.
coffers_vault_lens.bridge: The beam strikes the vault-eye and the bars grind back. Someone inside is already waiting for you.

detail.description: The vault sits behind a lock of light, a sunbeam bent down through a row of mirrors that someone has knocked crooked. Turn the mirrors to thread the beam through all three vault-eyes at once and the bars slide back.

coffers_ledger.flavor: The vault isn't full of gold. It's full of the Finndicate's books, and one of them is a log of every heading you've sailed since the coast. Somebody's been keeping track.

scene.text: The bars grind back. There's no gold inside. Just paper: shelf after shelf of the Finndicate's books, and one chained open on a stand in the middle.
It's not a ledger. It's a log. Your log. Every heading you've sailed since the coast, in someone else's hand.
The reef coast. The Gullet. The harbor gate. Each one written down the same hour you got there.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: We've been tracked.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Hmm...thought we were always looking behind our backs.
A voice behind you. You've heard it at every cache since the coast.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: Took your time, captain. Not that I ever lost you.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Wait...you're the shopkeeper that's shown up all throughout our journey. You work for the Finndicate?

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: A little demeaning referring to me as the shopkeeper.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: I'm the Don's Quartermaster. I make sure he's aware of all that's going on. And in order to do that...I have to be aware as well.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: The Don...?

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: That's right. The Don runs the Finndicate. But I arm the Don's crew. And I also let little sailors like yourself happen to come across free loot along the way. But of course I just use that to track your position at all times.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: Your reputation precedes you. You took a long way to get here. But alas, it must end here. The Don has to deal with more important things than you lot.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: What does the Finndicate want? Why are you hoarding resources?

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: The Don has his ways.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Guess we're gonna have to ask him directly then.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: Mark my words, you'll never see the Don...alive.

coffers_ledger.bridge: Every cache since the coast was the Quartermaster's, and every piece in them carried his tracker. That's how the Finndicate always knew where you were. Time to find it and rip it out.

detail.description: Past the vault-eye, the Coffers keep their real treasure: the Finndicate's books. Chained in the middle is a log of every move you've made since the coast, written down the hour you made it. Waiting beside it is the one who's armed you all along, and the reason they always knew where you were: the Quartermaster.
detail.summary: The Coffers' vault held a log of every heading you'd sailed since the coast. The Quartermaster was waiting. Every cache was his, and every piece he left you carried a tracker that told the Finndicate where you were.

preFightDialogue.speaker: narrator
preFightDialogue.text: The gun-deck is exactly as you left it, down to the lantern oil. The counter is still stocked. The keeper is still behind it, and you can see the shutters through him.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: The drowned keep better books than the living. Everything you left on my counter, everything you melted down since. I have it all, and I have *all the time there is*.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: Then you'll not mind us taking it back off you. Twice, if it comes to that.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: *They always come back.* That is the one thing I could ever count on.

phases.dialogueLine: Sink me? Lad, you already did. Try taking something off me instead.

check.name: The Salvage
check.telegraph: He swings a crane over the rail and hauls up the reinforced plating you never came back for. He means to wear it.
check.hint: Disrupt him. He cannot bolt it on if he cannot work.
check.counteredLine: The crane fouls and the plating goes back over the side. He does not take that well.
check.failLine: He bolts your plating over his own ribs and the holes close up.

phases.dialogueLine: You left the fire-shot on my counter. I have had a long time to think about where to put it.

check.name: The Long Burn
check.telegraph: He packs the incendiary you passed over and stands there holding a lit match, in no hurry at all.
check.hint: Survive it. Get a barrier up, or be ready to put the fire out.
check.counteredLine: The shot bursts against the barrier and burns itself out on open water.
check.failLine: Your own fire-shot goes through the deck and the ship starts to cook.

phases.dialogueLine: Every captain I ever armed, I watched sink. I always did keep the good glass back.

check.name: The Called Shot
check.telegraph: He raises your Gunner's Sight to a dead eye, takes the bearing off your own compass, and holds it. He does not need to hurry.
check.hint: Defend. Put something between you and a shot that is already aimed.
check.counteredLine: The shot lands where your hull was and finds a braced wall instead. He mutters something about waste.
check.failLine: He fires down your own sights. The shot goes exactly where he meant it to.

phases.dialogueLine: The don said bring him your colors. He never said in one piece.

check.name: The Death Roll
check.telegraph: Sal takes your hull in his teeth, sets his feet against the swell, and starts to turn.
check.hint: He is going to roll, and he will not let go. Only a crew ability gets something between your hull and that grip. Your own brace or dodge does nothing here.
check.counteredLine: He rolls against braced timber, tears off a mouthful of nothing, and lets go spitting splinters.
check.failLine: He rolls, and he keeps rolling, and your hull comes apart along the grain.

phases.dialogueLine: You want the Don? Then come through me. Nothing you carry gets past me.

preFightDialogue.speaker: narrator
preFightDialogue.text: The fog thickens until sea and sky blur into dull gray. Out of it, a slow-built ship glides up. Decks stacked with rolled charts and brass-bound sextants.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: I heard a young captain was reading my routes.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: It's him. The Finndicate's chartmaker.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: I prefer to be called The Cartographer. Has a nicer ring to it. You cut off my supply line from Krust. It's unfortunate, he was easy to work with. If a bit naive.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: No matter. The charts are nearly complete. I won't have time to entertain you any longer.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: Entertain us? We were just about to show YOU a good time.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: Me? You won't even be able to reach me. That's us chartmakers... always playing in the background.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: Why are you working for the Finndicate at all?

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: Mm... we've got bigger goals than those tiny brains of yours can even comprehend. Now if you'll excuse me.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: We're not letting him get away. Let's show him that pen and paper can't do what a cannon can.

phases.dialogueLine: Plate that outlived its own bones. Do you know how long I waited to wear this?
You have never once been fast enough. Let me show you what fast is.
You have put more iron through me than most captains see in a lifetime. Look at me.
I have been reading you since your first cast. There is nothing left of you I have not written down.
One last ride, captain. You landed this one yourself. Let us see you do it twice.

check.name: The Maw
check.telegraph: The don’s hull ROLLS, and keeps rolling, a jaw the size of your broadside opening under the waterline.
check.hint: A bite that wide can’t be weaved. Harden the hull with a brace, or blast the jaw apart with a big shot before it shuts.
check.counteredLine: Your crew throws the maw off its line and it grinds iron instead of deck.
check.failLine: The maw closes on your hull and something structural gives. Every blow after this one finds the gap.

phases.dialogueLine: There it is. The blood. Now the whole ocean knows where you are.

check.name: Blood in the Water
check.telegraph: He rakes a long gash down your hull and circles wide, the sea reddening with every pass at the smell of it.
check.hint: The wound is what keeps drawing him. Close it with a heal, or snare him off the blood-trail before he circles back in.
check.counteredLine: Your crew answers the wound and the blood-trail goes cold; he loses the scent.
check.failLine: He follows the blood straight in, tears the gash wider, and the wound feeds him.

phases.dialogueLine: Order isn't asked for, captain. It's TAKEN.

check.name: The Sounding
check.telegraph: The megalodon SOUNDS. The whole sea dips as he goes deep, gathering water for a breach that will land on your deck.
check.hint: You can’t block a falling mountain. You have to break the dive itself. Snare him out of it, or blast him up early with a big shot.
check.counteredLine: The dive breaks. He breaches early, wide, and the wave takes the blow for you.
check.failLine: The sea goes still. Then it goes UP, and the breach leaves your ship reeling and slow to answer.

phases.dialogueLine: Down here, everything answers to someone. Even me.

check.name: The Undertow
check.telegraph: He circles fast and low and the whole drowned court fires down the whirlpool at once, a wall of iron closing on your hull.
check.hint: No brace holds against a wall this wide. Raise a shield to break it, or out-heal what gets through.
check.counteredLine: The barrage breaks on your crew’s answer in a wall of spray.
check.failLine: The undertow drags your broadside off true, and the court’s iron rakes you while your guns swing wild.

phases.dialogueLine: Sink me if you can. The mission goes on WITHOUT me.

check.name: The Last Bite
check.telegraph: The megalodon rears his whole bulk from the water for one final lunge. And for one breath his throat hangs open above your deck.
check.hint: The throat hangs open for one breath. Fire everything down it with a big shot, or throw up a brace or shield and ride out the lunge.
check.counteredLine: Your crew fires straight down his throat and the last bite dies in the water.
check.failLine: The last bite comes down, and the deep finally closes over you.
